checks.name: containment-proof-detail
checks.summary: Real child process run via ProcessSupervisor{Confine: &NamespaceConfinement{Workspace: ws}}. Observed and asserted from the child's own captured marker files (not inferred from exit code alone): (1) write inside workspace succeeds (exit 0, file created). (2) write to a sibling path under the same top-level ancestor, outside workspace, fails; the child's own stderr, captured verbatim, reads 'outside/outside.txt: Read-only file system' (EROFS surfaced by the kernel through dash's own redirection-failure message). (3) positive control: the identical write, same paths, run via a plain ProcessSupervisor{} with no Confine, succeeds -- ruling out 'that path was never writable anyway'. (4) after ProcessSupervisor.Run returns (the ephemeral mount namespace already torn down by the kernel), the outside file still does not exist -- checked both immediately after the confined failure and again after the process exited.

checks.summary: ProcessSupervisor.Run refuses to start the child at all (no marker file is ever created) when NamespaceConfinement cannot be legitimately set up, proving the non-goal 'never silently run unconfined' rather than merely documenting it.
